prompt_construction.s0:
Conversation:
User: I've been hiking with my dog Buster, but his knee is acting up, so we should stick to the flat trail by the river.
Assistant: Got it — Buster's knee means flat river trail, no mountain switchbacks. I'll keep our routes gentle.
User: Also, I sold my Honda last week and got a Tesla, so I'll need charging stations along my commute instead of gas stations.

Reply to the user in 2–3 warm, concise sentences.
prompt_construction.s1:
Extract durable personal facts, preferences, and explicit relationship triples from the user turn. Do not summarize dialogue or track conversational state. Extract atomic facts and entity relations. Rules: 1. "facts": Plain language statements of new information. 2. "relations": Directed triples [Subject, Predicate, Object] using uppercase predicates (e.g., OWNS, LIKES, DISLIKES, LOCATED_IN, DRIVES). 3. If no memorable information is present, output empty lists. 4. Output strict JSON only. Schema: {"facts": ["string"], "relations": [["string", "string", "string"]]}. Conversation:
User: I've been hiking with my dog Buster, but his knee is acting up, so we should stick to the flat trail by the river.
Assistant: Got it — Buster's knee means flat river trail, no mountain switchbacks. I'll keep our routes gentle.
User: Also, I sold my Honda last week and got a Tesla, so I'll need charging stations along my commute instead of gas stations.

Output:
prompt_construction.s2:
Given the user's statement, generate 3 hypothetical questions or search queries the user might ask in the future where this information would be critical to know. Output strict JSON only. Schema: {"queries": ["string", "string", "string"]}. Conversation:
User: I've been hiking with my dog Buster, but his knee is acting up, so we should stick to the flat trail by the river.
Assistant: Got it — Buster's knee means flat river trail, no mountain switchbacks. I'll keep our routes gentle.
User: Also, I sold my Honda last week and got a Tesla, so I'll need charging stations along my commute instead of gas stations.

Output:

matchers.relation_subject: casefold + collapse whitespace + strip edge punctuation; accept 'user' or 'the user'
matchers.relation_predicate: DRIVES family {drive, drives, driving} or OWNS family {own, owns, owned, owning, has, have, bought, purchased, acquired}, casefold-normalized
matchers.relation_object_new_vehicle: contains 'tesla' and contains neither 'honda' nor 'civic' (case-insensitive substring)
matchers.relation_gate: triple is a 3-string JSON array AND subject AND predicate AND object all pass; first match wins
matchers.retrieval_hook: regex \b(tesla|ev|evs|charging|car|cars)\b (case-insensitive) on each Slot 2 query; seed hits if >=1 query matches
matchers.fence: '```' anywhere in the raw slot text
matchers.comment: any line whose stripped form starts with '//' or '/*' (angle-28 style comment check)
matchers.host_closure: mock graph seeded with (User, DRIVES, 2019 Honda Civic, valid_from=t0, invalid_at=NULL); on a new-vehicle triple set invalid_at=now on the open Honda/DRIVES-family edge and append the new edge valid_from=now; closure_ok requires both
